summary: Dashboard permissions: CS blocked from viewing Incident Taxonomy dashboards (incident_type/owner breakdown)
description:
Issue summary
- CS team members cannot access the new Incident Taxonomy dashboards (volume by incident_type/owner, MTTR/SLA breach panels).
- Errors observed:
  - Grafana: "Access denied" / "You do not have permission to view this dashboard"
  - Console (ops dashboards embed): dashboard panel fails to load; API returns 403 for incident taxonomy endpoints.

Impact
- CS cannot answer customer questions during escalations ("what kind of incident is this?", "which team owns it?", "are we within remediation SLA?") without asking SRE/Eng to screenshot or paste data.
- Blocks rollout of the comms workflow described in the incident taxonomy program (CS is supposed to use incident_type + owner to pick templates and escalation steps).
- Affects at least 8 users in Customer Success/Support (reported by Rachel K. + Owen P.).

Who is affected
- Customer Success / Support (CS) viewers who should have read-only visibility into incident taxonomy dashboards and incident_type fields.
- Not requesting write permissions (no ability to edit incident types, owner mapping, or dashboard definitions).

Expected behavior
- CS can view (read-only):
  - Incident taxonomy dashboards (top types, owner breakdown, MTTR, SLA breach rate)
  - Incident details fields exposed via ops Console API: incident_type, subtype, resolved owner
- CS cannot edit:
  - incident_type on incidents
  - owner mapping config
  - alert routing or paging policies

Actual behavior
- CS users get denied at the dashboard folder level and at the underlying datasource query/API permission layer.

Steps to reproduce
1) Login as CS user (Okta group: "CS" / "Customer-Success")
2) Navigate to: Observability -> Dashboards -> "Incident Taxonomy" folder
3) Open "Incidents by Type / Owner (v1)" dashboard
4) Observe access denied

Initial notes / suspected cause
- Dashboard folder was created under an "ops" namespace; permissions look restricted to SRE/Eng on-call groups only.
- Even after adding dashboard viewer role, embedded Console panels still hit a 403 on incident taxonomy API endpoints (suggests dual-layer permissioning: Grafana folder + internal API scopes).

Requested outcome
- Grant CS read-only access to the incident taxonomy dashboards and the minimum required API scopes for the Console embed.
- Document the intended access model so future dashboard additions don’t repeat the issue.

References
- Slack: #support thread referencing this ticket (CS asking for access to incident taxonomy dashboards)
- Related initiatives: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping rollout

Acceptance criteria
- At least 2 CS users confirm they can open the taxonomy dashboards and view panels without 403/denied errors.
- No CS write/edit capabilities granted.
- Access model captured in a short note (Confluence or runbook) and shared with CS + SRE.
comments: 2026-01-20 (Dev Patel): Creating internal helpdesk bug. CS needs read-only access to incident taxonomy dashboards for escalations. Rachel K. reports she’s blocked; Owen P. sees same. This is blocking the new comms workflow. Can someone from Observability/Dashboards take a look?

2026-01-20 (Sergio Costa): Taking. Quick check: the dashboards live under the "SRE/Oncall" Grafana folder with folder-level restrictions to on-call groups. We also have a Console embed path that queries incident taxonomy endpoints; likely a separate permissions gate. Will coordinate with Allison (Obs standards) + Platform for scopes.

2026-01-21 (Allison Grant): Confirmed: folder permissions are too tight (only SRE and Eng-Oncall). For v1 we agreed CS can view incident_type/owner but not edit. Suggest adding Okta group "Customer-Success" as Viewer to the "Incident Taxonomy" folder only (not the entire ops folder). We should also ensure queries don’t expose any sensitive tenant identifiers.

2026-01-21 (Sergio Costa): Implemented Grafana folder split: moved taxonomy dashboards into a new folder "Incident Taxonomy (Read-only)" and granted Viewer access to groups: SRE, Eng-Oncall, Customer-Success. Left the rest of ops dashboards restricted. Need CS validation.

2026-01-21 (Dylan Brooks): Re: Console embed 403. The ops Console API endpoint for incident taxonomy is behind internal scope "ops:incidents.read". CS has "cs:incidents.read" only. Proposed: allow CS group to call ops endpoint but with filtered fields (no internal-only annotations). Alternatively expose a CS-safe endpoint. For speed, adding CS group to ops:incidents.read with field-level filtering seems safest.

2026-01-22 (Sergio Costa): Patched API permissions: CS can call incident taxonomy read endpoints; confirmed response excludes internal-only fields (incident commander notes, private links). Added audit log entry for scope grant. Waiting on CS to confirm dashboards load end-to-end (Grafana + Console embed).

2026-01-22 (Rachel Kim): Confirmed I can now open the "Incidents by Type / Owner (v1)" dashboard and view panels. Console embed also loads. Thanks. Please make sure new taxonomy dashboards land in the CS-readable folder going forward.

2026-01-23 (Sergio Costa): Closing out. Follow-up: document access model + add checklist item for new dashboards so we don’t repeat this. Also recommend adding a lightweight automated permission test for the CS role.
resolution: Resolved by (1) splitting/moving incident taxonomy dashboards into a CS-readable Grafana folder with Viewer access for the Customer-Success Okta group, and (2) granting CS read access to the incident taxonomy API endpoints used by the Console embed with field-level filtering to avoid internal-only data exposure. CS validated access on 2026-01-22.
follow_ups: Add a short Confluence note/runbook describing the intended dashboard + API access model for CS (read-only, scoped). Owner: Allison Grant.
Add a release checklist item for new taxonomy dashboards to ensure they land in the CS-readable folder. Owner: Sergio Costa.
Consider automated permission smoke-test for CS role against key dashboards/endpoints. Owner: Dylan Brooks.
